propositions: The generic reads-under-sync-contention property does not subsume test_cli_show_complete_or_erroring_under_write_burst because the original test detects partial-success faults (F3: empty valid JSON, F6: missing record fields) that the generic property misses.
Fault seeds F5 and F7 are caught only by the generic property (35s stall, empty list surface), proving neither oracle subsumes the other and both provide unique detection value.

Reverting the slim-fetch-ledge fix leaves both burst tests green; only the deterministic held-lock tests (T1, T4) detect the actual regression, indicating the burst test's protection value comes from payload-completeness assertions, not from the concurrent write storm.

The consolidation candidate test costs 57.6s per change in aggregate runner time (12.79-14.93s Ubuntu, 15.34s macOS), but removal forfeits F3/F6 detection and is not available on the deletion path per mutation-testing criterion (Just et al. FSE 2014).

The original test adds a content-completeness assertion (doc.get('ticket_id')) beyond the generic test's shape-validation (isinstance(doc, expected_shape)), constituting a uniquely-held detection class for the partial-success half of the original regression.
